tasks.title: Short Questions
tasks.statement: Show, in a few steps in the writing sheets, your method of solution. Write your final answers in the answer sheets provided. Partial credits will be given for answers without showing method of solution.

parts.question: For an observer at latitude 42.5o N and longitude 71o W, estimate the time of sun rise on 21 December if the observer’s civil time is - 5 hours from GMT. Ignore refraction of the atmosphere and the size of the solar disc.
parts.reference: Ans. 7:10 am (or 7:18 am via alternative calculation).

parts.question: The largest angular separation between Venus and the Sun, when viewed from the Earth, is 46o . Calculate the radius of Venus’s circular orbit in A.U.
parts.reference: R = R⊕ sin 46o = 1 A.U. sin 46o = 0.72 A.U.

parts.question: The time interval between noon on 1 July and noon on 31 December is 183 solar days. What is this interval in sidereal days?
One night during a full Moon, the Moon subtends an angle of 0.46 degree to an observer. What is the observer’s distance to the Moon on that night?

An observer was able to measure the difference in the directions, due to the Earth’s motion around the Sun, to a star as distant as 100 parsecs away. What was the minimum angular difference in arc seconds this observer could measure?
A Sun-orbiting periodic comet is the farthest at 31.5 A.U. and the closest at 0.5 A.U.. What is the orbital period of this comet?
For the comet in question 1.6, what is the area (in square A.U. per year) swept by the line joining the comet and the Sun?
At what wavelength does a star with the surface temperature of 4000 K emit most intensely?

Calculate the total luminosity of a star whose surface temperature is 7500 K, and whose radius is 2.5 times that of our Sun. Give your answer in units of the solar luminosity, assuming the surface temperature of the Sun to be 5800 K.
A K star on the Main Sequence has a luminosity of 0.4 L_sun. This star is observed to have a flux of 6.23 × 10^-14 W.m^-2. What is the distance to this star? You may neglect the atmospheric effect.
A supernova shines with a luminosity 10^10 times that of the Sun. If such a supernova appears in our sky as bright as the Sun, how far away from us must it be located?

The (spin-flip) transition of atomic hydrogen at rest generates the electromagnetic wave of the frequency nu_0 = 1420.406 MHz. Such an emission from a gas cloud near the galactic center is observed to have a frequency nu = 1421.65 MHz. Calculate the velocity of the gas cloud. Is it moving towards or away from the Earth?
A crater on the surface of the Moon has a diameter of 80 km. Is it possible to resolve this crater with naked eyes, assuming the eye pupil aperture is 5 mm?
parts.reference: D_min = 2.9 mm, yes, it is possible

parts.question: If the Sun were to collapse gravitationally to form a non-rotating black hole, what would be its event horizon (its Schwarzschild radius)?

The magnitude of the faintest star you can see with naked eyes is m = 6, whereas that of the brightest star in the sky is m = -1.5. What is the energy-flux ratio of the faintest to that of the brightest?

tasks.title: A Planet & its Surface Temperature
tasks.statement: Let us consider a planet of radius R, revolving in a circular orbit of radius a at a distance D from its star of luminosity L. It is assumed to be a black body, in equilibrium, totally absorbing all the radiation from the star, radiating as a spherical body at the same temperature, and neglecting its internal source of energy.

parts.question: What is the radiation flux from the star at the planet’s surface? (1 point)
What is the total rate of energy, intercepted by the planet, radiating as a black body? (1 point)
parts.reference: A = (1 - alpha) * pi * R^2 * I = (1 - alpha) * L * R^2 / (4 * D^2)

parts.question: What is the reradiating luminosity of the planet? (1 point)
What is the equivalent black-body surface temperature of the planet? (1 point)
If we were to assume that only the side of the planet is-continually facing the star, what would be the equivalent surface temperature of that side? (1 point)
For the planet in puffup orbit given: a = 0.25, D = 1.523 A.U., compute its surface temperature in kelvins for the value of L = 3.826 * 10^26 W. (2 points for final numeric value)

tasks.title: Binary System
tasks.statement:
Let us consider a binary system of two stars of masses M1 and M2 at a distance D. M1 and M2 are dynamically stable, moving in circular orbits with an angular velocity omega about their common centre of mass. When viewed at right angles, passing eclipses give periodic eclipses due to the stars occulting each other.
    In order to make it mathematically simple, we will assume that the stars are point particles and that the effects of the relativity about their own spins are the negligible.

parts.question: What is the total orbital angular momentum and kinetic energy of the system? (2 points)
Find the relation between the angular velocity omega and the distance D between the stars. (1 point)
In a time duration Dt, a mass transfer between the two stars results in a change of mass DM1 in M1, find the fraction Dw in terms of omega, D and DM1. (2 points)

In a certain binary system, M1 = 2.9 M_sun, M2 = 1.4 M_sun and the orbital period, T = 2.49 days. If T has increased by 20 s in the past 100 years, find the sign of (DM1 / (M1 * Dt)) in the last part century. (2.5 points)
In which direction is mass outflowing, from M1 to M2, or M2 to M1? (1.5 points)
parts.reference: Mass is flowing from M2 to M1.

parts.question: Find also the sign of (DD / Dt) in the last part century. (1 point)

tasks.title: Gravitational Lensing
tasks.statement: Gravitational lensing is a phenomenon in which a massive object deflects a light ray from a distant source to the terrestrial observer at distance DS in a cosmic space. An astronomy group observed that a distant point source produced twin line images due to a foreground galaxy acting as a gravitational lens at distance DL. This gravitational field was considered of 1 solar mass.

parts.question: Find what is the radius of the star from the Earth at the planet’s surface? (2 points)
parts.reference: theta^2 - beta * theta = (4GM / c^2) * ((DS - DL) / (DL * DS)). For beta = 0, theta_E = sqrt((4GM / c^2) * ((DS - DL) / (DL * DS))).

parts.question: What is the theta_E angle of star, situated at 50 kpc, when L is situated at 10 kpc distance from the lens? (1 point)
What is the resolution of the Hubble Space Telescope with 2.4 m diameter? (2 points)
parts.reference: theta_Hubble = 2.54 * 10^-7 radian. Hubble telescope could not resolve this Einstein ring.

parts.question: What is the position of the Dürrenmatt surface reflection concerning 9.5 d stationary dots? (2 points)
parts.reference: theta_1,2 = (beta / 2) +- sqrt((beta / 2)^2 + theta_E^2). Two images for a single isolated source.

parts.question: In Figure 1, if an illustrated points require M_1 and M_2 situated at M_1 and M_2 sources of the cosmological lens. Find the positions theta_1 and theta_2 of the two images. In terms of beta and theta_E. (2 points)
Find finally the ratios of magnifications dI / d beta in terms of eta, when d_B = beta and d_A = alpha. (1 point)
